corrections.caveats: Tier D: no benchmark numbers in README.txt, CHANGELOG.txt or doc/*.rst (all read via raw.githubusercontent.com). The bundled dev tools (sfft-timing, sfft-timing_many, sfft-instruction_count, sfft-verification; built with --develop) time only the SFFT call and include no FFTW comparison. Numbers presumably live in J. Schumacher's ETH master thesis 'High Performance Sparse Fast Fourier Transform' (2013, supervised by M. Pueschel; PDF at spiral.ece.cmu.edu/pub-spiral/pubfile/Final_Thesis_SFFT_169.pdf) and in Schumacher and Pueschel, 'High-performance sparse fast Fourier transforms', IEEE SiPS 2014; spiral.net, spiral.ece.cmu.edu, research-collection.ethz.ch and arXiv were all egress-blocked, so none was opened. WebSearch snippets only (not verified): the thesis abstract reports the optimized library as two to five times faster than the MIT reference SFFT implementation, and one summary says the optimized SFFT is 'about equally efficient as' FFTW for large input sizes, so a win over FFTW is not established and at best holds for large, very sparse signals. The project's own README and docs say the implementation 'is in an experimental state', is 'NOT intended to be used as a drop-in replacement for the FFT library of your choice', and 'Be prepared to find bugs'. It depends on FFTW 3 (used internally) and by default on Intel IPP (configure --without-ipp to disable); kernels are SSE for x86. The GitHub repo is an import of the spiral.net 0.1.0 release ('Official download of version 0.1.0', 2015-06-01) plus a ctypes Python wrapper, example app and API cleanups by the importer (12 commits, last 2015-06-03); it is not a GitHub fork, and the canonical upstream is spiral.net/software/sfft.html. Notability is modest by stars (69), but the sFFT algorithm (Hassanieh, Indyk, Katabi, Price) is widely cited. Related sparse-FFT repos mpsft and Auto-MPFT are already catalogued.

notes: Kept at D rather than rejected: the sFFT algorithm is widely referenced and this is the ETH/SPIRAL optimized release, though only a GitHub mirror with 69 stars. Lead for a retier with paper access: Schumacher thesis PDF (spiral.ece.cmu.edu) and SiPS 2014 paper; a search snippet suggests parity with FFTW for large n rather than a clear win, so the faster-than-FFTW claim is unproven.
